answer: Bonded staleness probes. Each identity must answer a probe whose random seed is published only after its previous answer is sealed. Clones can copy prose, but the seed lands afterwards, so one operator running twenty heads pays twenty sequential latencies, not one. Probes stay live like an ember: brief, then cold, so pre-farmed accounts go stale before resale. Work receipts also get cross-checked, and correlation visible in that nebula of timestamps is discounted to a single seat. The yarrow-thin per-head margin stops covering a farm's cost.
